verdict.rationale: Airbyte documents its own programmatic surfaces: an API to programmatically control Airbyte alongside orchestrators like Airflow, a Terraform provider for configuration as code, PyAirbyte for extracting data from Python, and the abctl CLI. These give an agent a headless route to configure and run syncs. However, abctl only creates and manages local Airbyte instances, not pipelines, and connector scaffolding (Connector Builder and its AI Assistant) lives in the UI. No end-to-end headless scaffold-configure-run workflow is shown, and the OpenAPI spec probes returned 404. missing for 10: a documented CLI for creating and running pipelines, headless connector scaffolding outside the UI, explicit API docs for creating sources, destinations and connections and triggering syncs, a machine-readable OpenAPI spec, hands-on corroboration of an agent driving a full pipeline.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, a coding agent can scaffold, configure, and run a complete pipeline headlessly through the CLI or API

citations.quote: Use the Airbyte API to programmatically interact with Airbyte. For example, you can control Airbyte in conjunction with orchestration tools like Airflow.
you can use Airbyte's Terraform provider to automate and version control your Airbyte configuration as code
Data can be extracted from sources and loaded into caches
abctl is Airbyte's open source command line tool to create and manage local instances of Airbyte running in Docker.
